# tomabel.ee

> Tom Kristian Abel — security researcher and systems architect. I reverse engineer how authentication and browser defenses fail, then design the systems that survive what I find.

Based in Estonia. Writes in English and Estonian. Research focuses on identity protocols (FIDO2 / WebAuthn, eIDAS, Smart-ID), anti-fraud VMs, TLS fingerprinting, and zero-trust architecture. Findings go to the vendor first, then to regulators (RIA, TTJA, AKI) where needed.

## Pages

- [Home](https://tomabel.ee/): Hero, featured research and systems, recent essays.
- [Research](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/): Research, teardowns, frameworks, and essays in one index (client-side filter tabs).
  - [BotGuard, disassembled — reverse engineering Google's anti-fraud VM](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/botguard-disassembled/): a teardown from public research of the bytecode VM and its anti-debugging and obfuscation layers, with an unreproduced 2021 note on where token binding stops. Not reported to Google.
  - [The Achilles' heel of Estonia's e-state — Smart-ID / eID research](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/smart-id-achilles-heel/): why the protocol resists MITM and endpoint attacks by design, how the approval layer fails instead, and the interactive signing-relay class of attack against Smart-ID+ cross-device QR flows. Reported to SK ID Solutions in November 2025, then to RIA, TTJA and AKI in April 2026.
  - [Zero-Trust Octagon — a framework from first principles](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/zero-trust-octagon/): 8 axioms, a 9-dimension morphological matrix, and archetypal breach walkthroughs.
  - [PACT and the software-anchor turn — a critical analysis of Private Access Control Tokens](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/pact-software-anchor-turn/): why Cloudflare's PACT proposal moves trust from hardware anchors to issuer judgment, and why the missing governance layer decides whether the web gets an open anti-bot layer or another trust oligopoly.
  - [The PIN that cannot be delegated — Smart-ID, AI agents, and eIDAS](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/the-pin-that-cannot-be-delegated/): why an AI agent cannot enter your Smart-ID PIN — SK's own terms, the remote-QSCD practice statement, and eIDAS Articles 26 and 32 side by side, and the OAuth-style delegation pattern that works.
  - [I used to break authentication. Here's what that taught me about building it.](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/i-used-to-break-authentication/): the thesis essay — why understanding offense is a prerequisite for credible defense, worked through one Smart-ID relay example.
  - [What client-side trust is actually worth](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/what-client-side-trust-is-actually-worth/): the BotGuard teardown as a case study for why any defense running on a machine you don't control is a claim, not a proof — and what to build instead.
  - [The kratt problem](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/the-kratt-problem/): offensive capability as Estonian folklore — a servant that works tirelessly while pointed and turns on its maker when idle; ethics as a pointing problem.
  - [Coordinated disclosure in a small country](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/coordinated-disclosure-in-a-small-country/): what disclosing a flaw in critical digital infrastructure looks like in Estonia, where everyone knows each other — the legal exposure, the incentives, and why owning your story in public is the protection that scales.
  - [The fix that doesn't need SK](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/the-fix-that-doesnt-need-sk/): the Achilles' heel report's five fixes all need a regulator, the banks, or a legislature or court to move — a sixth, checking each session against the account's device and network history at a bank's own edge, doesn't. Strongest against attacker-session vishing and the cross-device relay.
  - [ChatGPT is not a phishing scanner](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/chatgpt-is-not-a-phishing-scanner/): a fact check of the "paste the suspicious link into ChatGPT" advice — what ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini actually document, why TDS and AI-targeted cloaking can serve an assistant's fetch a decoy page, and why VirusTotal and Google's Safe Browsing site status are a better first check, though not a final verdict.
  - [The evolution of cyber fraud in Estonia, 2017–2026](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/the-evolution-of-cyber-fraud-in-estonia/): how Estonia's small language held the fraud industry at arm's length, and what happened when the barrier fell in late 2024 — recruited native speakers, industrialized vishing call centers, courier networks, and AI deepfakes, with annual losses climbing to €29 million in 2025.
  - [The Gray Space: Russian-Linked Proxy and Hosting Infrastructure in Estonia](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/russian-cyber-ops-estonia-hosting/): an OSINT reference on the Fineproxy network and QualityNetwork OÜ's 2026 RIPE allocation, what the record shows about Vault Dweller OÜ's withdrawn AS203834, and why none of it is proven Russian state activity.
  - [How client-side anti-fraud actually works, and what VLM agents change](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/why-vlms-break-client-side-anti-fraud/): how client-side anti-fraud actually works, why the old arms race was about forgery, and what changes when a vision-language model drives a real browser — plus which of the five paradigms survive and the attestation centralization problem.
  - [The Nine Dimensions of Zero Trust](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/nine-dimensions-of-zero-trust/): the nine-dimension morphological matrix laid out axis by axis — what each dimension decides, the realistic range of positions, and why "are we zero trust?" is the wrong question.
  - [The Fortune 500 Illusion of Control](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/the-fortune-500-illusion-of-control/): a step-by-step breach trace of Archetype B — the enterprise with the largest budget and the most attestations — from stolen session cookie to full database export, compressed into about twenty minutes. Analytical composite, not a real incident.
  - [Move Fast, Fix It In Prod: A Full Breach Trace of the Startup Archetype](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/move-fast-fix-it-in-prod/): the full supply-chain and CI/CD trace for Archetype C: dependency to pipeline to credential to production, and why the automation that makes a startup fast is what makes the blast radius large.
  - [SaaS-Glued Lean Defense: The Full Breach Trace for Archetype D](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/saas-glued-lean-defense/): the composite breach trace for one operator and a dozen SaaS products: MFA fatigue, the OAuth grant cascade, and six fixes that need an afternoon rather than a budget.
  - [Identity Is the Root. Proof Is the Gate.](https://tomabel.ee/disclosures/identity-is-the-root-proof-is-the-gate/): the capstone argument connecting the zero-trust work to the eID research: every control is downstream of identity, a login is a point-in-time assertion, and the approval layer is where real systems fail.
- [Systems](https://tomabel.ee/systems/): Shipped systems — fingerprintproxy (production Go TLS-fingerprinting proxy, 65+ browser profiles, JA3/JA4), Vooglaadija (FastAPI media-extraction service with Redis queues, JWT auth, observability), Discord RAG pipeline (LanceDB + BM25 hybrid retrieval with RBAC-aware filtering).
- [About](https://tomabel.ee/about/): Bio, philosophy, and the kratt metaphor.
- [My story](https://tomabel.ee/my-story/): How I got here, in three acts — the criminal case, the pivot from offense to research, and the published work as evidence. Links the original Delfi interview.
- [Privacy Policy](https://tomabel.ee/privacy/), [Terms of Service](https://tomabel.ee/terms/), [Security Research Policy](https://tomabel.ee/disclosure/)
